blocks.title: Computational biology
blocks.text: Computational biology is an interdisciplinary field that uses computational techniques and tools to solve biological problems. It integrates knowledge from biology, computer science, mathematics and statistics to analyse and interpret biological data.

Its importance lies in its ability to handle large data sets, uncover hidden patterns and generate predictive models that can lead to new biological insights and applications. Its major areas are genomics, proteomics and bioinformatics.

items: Genomics is the study of genomes, the complete set of DNA within a single cell of an organism. It involves sequencing, assembling and analysing the function and structure of genomes, and helps in understanding genetic variations, gene function and evolutionary relationships.

Proteomics is the large-scale study of proteins, including their structures and functions. It aims to map the entire set of proteins (the proteome) produced by an organism and to understand their interactions and roles in cellular processes.
Bioinformatics is the application of computer technology to manage and analyse biological data. Its tools and techniques store, retrieve and analyse DNA, RNA and protein sequences.

Drug discovery: computational biology helps identify potential drug targets and simulates the effects of drugs on biological systems, accelerating drug discovery by predicting how drugs interact with proteins and other molecules.
Genetic research: by analysing DNA sequences it identifies genetic variations associated with diseases, aids understanding of the genetic basis of disease, and can lead to personalised medicine.
Evolutionary biology: computational tools compare genetic information across species, helping to reconstruct evolutionary relationships and understand the process of evolution.

GenBank is a comprehensive public database of nucleotide sequences with supporting bibliographic and biological annotations. It gives access to a vast repository of DNA sequences from many organisms, facilitating genetic research and comparative genomics.

The Protein Data Bank (PDB) provides 3D structural data of large biological molecules such as proteins and nucleic acids. It is important for studying the structures of macromolecules, understanding their functions and designing drugs that target specific protein structures.

Ensembl is a genome browser providing information on genome sequences, gene models and comparative genomics for various species. It helps to access and visualise genomic data, supporting genomics and evolutionary biology.

BLAST (Basic Local Alignment Search Tool) compares primary biological sequence information, such as the amino acid sequences of proteins or the nucleotides of DNA. It helps identify homologous sequences, predict the functions of unknown genes and study evolutionary relationships.

FASTA is a sequence alignment tool that compares a query sequence to a database of sequences to find regions of similarity. It is used for searching protein and nucleotide databases, identifying sequence homology and analysing sequence alignments.

blocks.long_description: Computational biology combines biology, computer science, mathematics and statistics. Its areas are genomics, the whole DNA of a cell; proteomics, all the proteins an organism makes; and bioinformatics, the storing, retrieving and analysing of sequences. Its key databases are GenBank for nucleotide sequences, the Protein Data Bank for 3D structures and Ensembl as a genome browser; its key algorithms BLAST and FASTA find similar sequences. It is applied to drug discovery, genetic research and evolutionary biology.
